newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico publishes rules for derivatives market.
newsitem.headline: Mexico publishes rules for derivatives market.

text.p: The Mexican Stock Exchange late Wednesday announced rules for the creation of a futures and options derivatives market.
The regulations provide the basic framework for the derivatives market, such as setting down rules about how traders can operate and how trades are regulated, the exchange said in a statement.
The Mexican Bourse of Derivative Products will be known as MexDer and the clearing and regulating house for derivative trades will be known as Asigna.
MexDer will be self-regulating and Asigna will be a trusteeship with at least five partners, either banks or brokerages, the Mexican bourse said.
"The objective of Asigna will be to compensate and liquidate futures contracts and options carried out on MexDer and act as a counterpart in all operations," it added.

In the first phase of the development of the MexDer, futures and options will be able to be traded against the IPC index of stocks, foreign exchange contracts and the secondary money market, namely Cetes, which are Mexican T-bills.
Manuel Robleda, chairman of the Mexican Stock Exchange, said in December that the MexDer would be operational in the second half of 1997.
